content:
The Associated Press has called the Texas U.S. Senate race for Democrat James Talarico, who defeated Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. CNN, NBC News and Decision Desk HQ also projected the race for Talarico on election night.

With 67.49 percent of precincts reporting statewide, Talarico led with 4,155,536 votes, or about 59.1 percent, to Paxton's 2,767,417 votes, or about 39.3 percent, according to the Associated Press. Libertarian Ted Brown had 112,103 votes, or about 1.6 percent.

Talarico, a Democratic state representative from Austin, will become the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from Texas since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. Paxton, the state's attorney general, was seeking the seat being vacated by Sen. John Cornyn.

In Webb County, Talarico led Paxton 33,033 votes to 10,890 votes, with 65.82 percent of the county's precincts reporting, according to the Associated Press.

The results remain unofficial until they are canvassed and certified.

  • Associated Press — Texas U.S. Senate election results, November 3, 2026
